task.title: Review network exposure and proxy-readiness questions
task.shortdesc: Prepare network exposure notes and reverse-proxy questions without publishing unsupported TLS or proxy recipes as BPM 0.9.0 behavior.

prereq.p: The current single-node source readiness assessment is complete, and the operator knows whether users will reach BPM through loopback, a WSL forwarded address, a lab host, or an externally owned proxy.

context.p: BPM can run on a configured host and port, but BPM 0.9.0 documentation does not provide an official reverse proxy, TLS termination, authentication gateway, header policy, or rate-limiting recipe.

step.cmd: Choose the smallest network exposure that satisfies the current evaluation.

info.p: Prefer 127.0.0.1. Use BPM_HOST="0.0.0.0" only when WSL forwarding or a controlled lab network requires it, and record why BPM_PORT="8000" is reachable.

step.cmd: Write down proxy-readiness questions before adding any external proxy.

info.p: Answer who owns TLS certificates, hostname routing, request size limits, timeout values, CORS origins through BPM_CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS, forwarded headers, access logs, and incident response. These questions can be prepared now; the official TLS/proxy recipes are planned but not implemented yet.

step.cmd: Verify that probes still work through the chosen boundary.

info.p: If an externally owned proxy is used in a lab, record both direct source probes and proxy-side probes. Do not treat a proxy 200 response as proof of BPM authentication, authorization, or HA.

info.note: BPM 0.9.0 does not ship packaged services, official TLS/proxy recipes, supported HA clustering, WAF rules, request signing, rate limiting, SSO, OAuth/OIDC, role-based access control, or production hardening. Keep those as external controls or deferred requirements.

result.p: The network note separates what can be configured now from reverse-proxy and TLS decisions that remain external or deferred.

postreq.p: Use the monitoring, backup, and update-window topic before a shared evaluation window starts.
